dzhng/jevgrep.why: Asks an LLM to judge relevance across folders, files and declarations, returning verbatim excerpts as a semantic starting point for agents; needs only Node and a provider key.

ZacharyZhang-NY/OmaPhoto.why: A from-scratch Linux port that reads and writes the original Compositor .comp projects and follows the Omarchy theme, so files move between it and the macOS app instead of being re-created.

DanFessler/trellis.why: Split into a framework-agnostic core with React and custom-element adapters, it keeps every nested panel mounted while users drag, split, float and zoom the workspace.

firelex/jeff.why: Returns a calibrated probability per option in a single forward pass, about 22ms, with no generated text to parse, and runs locally on small fine-tuned models you can retrain.

https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=498.why: Unlike the Python original, each agent is a supervised OTP process, and prompts are built from typed signatures so model replies are validated rather than parsed by hand.

jaydendavisnc/inkwave.why: Not a tech demo: it's a playable online 4v4 game with room codes, bots that backfill dropped players, and liquid-ink simulation, all in one HTML file with no build step.

seamusc/papermono-shopping-list.why: A complete, readable ~2,400-line firmware rather than a snippet, notable for handling e-paper partial-refresh ghosting and Wi-Fi duty-cycling so it can seed other firmware.

https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=498.why: Ships as a self-contained binary with vim keys, mouse and themes; built on OpenTUI and Effect, so it doubles as a readable example of an Effect-based terminal app.
A real client-side WebAssembly raster-plus-vector editor that runs without an account, positioned as a free alternative rather than another subscription design suite.
A 0.5B ternary model sliced across seven ESP32-S3 boards, attention and MLP on nodes, a master doing tokenization, linked in an SPI daisy-chain pipeline.
